findings.title: WmiPrvSE.exe without filesystem path — highest MRI score, already exited

peirce_chain.firstness: WmiPrvSE.exe (PID=2508) observed with parent svchost.exe (PID=656). MRI score 61.0 — highest in system. Process had already EXITED at time of memory acquisition. No filesystem path recorded in memory structures.
peirce_chain.secondness: WmiPrvSE.exe normally resides at C:\Windows\System32\wbem\WmiPrvSE.exe and spawns from svchost.exe (DcomLaunch group). Parent relationship is NORMAL. Missing path for an exited process CAN be a memory acquisition artifact — Windows may reclaim EPROCESS path information after process termination. However, MRI score of 61 is elevated. In context of same-day Zeus infection on adjacent host nromanoff (10.3.58.5), this warrants investigation.
peirce_chain.thirdness: WMI-based lateral movement (T1047) uses WmiPrvSE.exe as execution host for remote payloads. Pattern: attacker executes via WMI, payload runs inside WmiPrvSE, process exits after completion, path information not retained. However, this SAME pattern occurs with legitimate WMI queries (SCCM, GPO, monitoring). Single artifact insufficient to distinguish attack from administration.

findings.carnegie_pattern: None detected — system-level artifact, no social engineering component
findings.devil_advocate: WmiPrvSE.exe exits normally after completing WMI queries. Missing filesystem path is a documented behavior for exited processes in Windows 7 memory — the kernel reclaims EPROCESS structures. MRI score of 61 reflects the missing-path anomaly itself, not independent evidence of compromise. A SCCM inventory scan, GPO enforcement, or enterprise monitoring tool could produce this exact pattern. Without process memory dump or corroborating persistence artifact, benign WMI activity cannot be excluded.
findings.corroboration: No corroborating artifact found. No persistence binaries in Temp directories. No shimcache anomaly available. No prefetch data analyzed. Remains single-source INFERRED.

findings.title: PPID anomaly — csrss.exe/winlogon.exe parent shows spoolsv.exe (PID reuse artifact)

peirce_chain.firstness: csrss.exe (PID=440, MRI=58) and winlogon.exe (PID=480, MRI=47) both show ParentPID=432. PID 432 is currently occupied by spoolsv.exe (print spooler).
peirce_chain.secondness: csrss.exe and winlogon.exe are ALWAYS spawned by smss.exe — never by spoolsv.exe. This appears as a critical process tree anomaly. However, this is a DOCUMENTED Windows 7 memory forensics artifact: smss.exe session process creates csrss/winlogon, then terminates. The kernel assigns PID 432 to a new process (spoolsv.exe). The PPID field in csrss/winlogon still references the original PID 432 (now reused). This is PID recycling, not process injection.
peirce_chain.thirdness: No deliberate pattern. This is a well-documented forensic artifact in Windows process analysis. The MRI scores (58, 47) reflect the PPID anomaly itself but the anomaly has a complete benign explanation.

findings.devil_advocate: N/A — NOISE verdict, refutation not required
findings.corroboration: PID reuse is independently documented in Windows 7 memory forensics literature and confirmed by process tree analysis.

findings.title: lsass.exe RPC connections to unknown workstation 10.3.58.4 in breach subnet

peirce_chain.firstness: lsass.exe (PID=552) has CLOSED TCP connections to 10.3.58.4:135 (RPC endpoint mapper) and 10.3.58.4:49156 (RPC dynamic endpoint). Connection state is CLOSED — activity completed before acquisition.
peirce_chain.secondness: lsass.exe initiating outbound RPC to peer IP in same /24 as confirmed Zeus host (nromanoff 10.3.58.5). RPC endpoint mapper (port 135) followed by dynamic RPC (49156) is the standard Windows RPC connection pattern. This pattern is NORMAL for domain authentication (NTLM/Kerberos to a DC). It is ALSO consistent with credential relay, pass-the-hash (T1550.002), or remote service interaction. The critical unknown: is 10.3.58.4 a domain controller? If yes, this is entirely normal. If it is a peer workstation, it is anomalous.
peirce_chain.thirdness: In an active breach environment with confirmed Zeus on an adjacent host, lsass.exe RPC to an unidentified lateral IP raises the lateral movement hypothesis. However, without identifying 10.3.58.4 and without observing the authentication payload content, this remains a single-source indicator with a strong benign alternative.

findings.devil_advocate: lsass.exe connects to other hosts via RPC as part of NORMAL domain authentication. Every Kerberos ticket request, NTLM challenge-response, and group policy lookup generates lsass.exe outbound RPC. Port 135 (endpoint mapper) → dynamic port is the standard RPC handshake. 10.3.58.4 may be a domain controller, file server, or any domain member requiring mutual authentication. The connections are CLOSED — there is no active suspicious session. F-Response examiner also connected to 10.3.58.4:5681, suggesting the IR team knew about this host. Without identifying 10.3.58.4's role in the domain, credential relay cannot be distinguished from normal authentication.
findings.corroboration: No corroborating artifact. No authentication logs available. No shimcache or prefetch for lateral tools. Event logs not populated in .mans. Remains single-source.

habit_incongruence.override_reason: Daubert Corroboration Gate — single artifact, destination identity unknown, connections CLOSED

findings.title: RDP TCP 3389 listening — lateral movement surface during active breach

peirce_chain.firstness: TCP port 3389 (RDP) actively LISTENING on svchost.exe (PID=408). No active RDP sessions in memory snapshot.
peirce_chain.secondness: RDP listening is standard enterprise Windows configuration, especially for executive workstations requiring remote IT support. No active sessions means no one was connected via RDP at acquisition time.
peirce_chain.thirdness: RDP as a lateral movement surface (T1021.001) is contextually relevant during an active breach but the mere presence of a listening port without an active session or connection history is not an indicator of compromise. It is standard operational configuration.

findings.corroboration: Standard Windows enterprise configuration. No evidence of exploitation.

self_correction_events.target: F-001/F-003 habit_incongruence vs CAIE cross-tool consistency

checks_performed.reason: habit_incongruence treats all observed actions as anomalies without weighting against benign baselines. CAIE applies spoofability penalties and Noisy-OR fusion. CAIE adjusted score for WmiPrvSE=0.0826 (memory_process, spoofability=0.15). Habit tool over-reports when input descriptions contain contextual metadata (breach environment) as behavioral observations.

lsass.exe RPC to peer workstations is within normal domain authentication behavior. Connections were CLOSED at acquisition. CAIE network_flow spoofability=0.75 heavily penalizes this evidence class. Habit tool lacks domain auth baseline context.

infer_intent analyzes message-based communication trajectories. Forensic artifacts are system-level, not message-level. NOISE reflects tool inapplicability to this evidence class, not disagreement with habit analysis.

No evidence staging detected. If attacker had planted lateral movement artifacts, Eco would detect too-perfect alignment. Normal distribution supports genuine operational artifacts, not attack fabrication.

self_correction_events.resolution: No contradictions. 2 tool sensitivity limitations documented (habit_incongruence over-reports without corroboration weighting). CAIE composite 0.1381 is authoritative mathematical score. Verdicts capped per Daubert corroboration standard.
